title: Thyroid hormone levels of pregnant inuit women and their infants exposed to environmental contaminants.
ehr_evidence: We measured thyroid hormone parameters [thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), free thyroxine (fT4), total triiodothyronine (T3), thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG)] and concentrations of several contaminants [PCB-153, hydroxylated metabolites of PCBs (HO-PCBs), pentachlorophenol (PCP) and hexachlorobenzene (HCB)] in maternal plasma at delivery (n = 120), in umbilical cord plasma (n = 95), and in infant plasma at 7 months postpartum (n = 130).
summary: A prospective cohort study of pregnant Inuit women in Nunavik, Quebec, Canada and their infants, examining associations between exposure to organochlorine compounds (PCBs, HCB, PCP, HO-PCBs) and thyroid hormone status in mothers and infants during the first year of life.
key_findings: Positive association between HO-PCBs and T3 concentrations in pregnant women (β = 0.57, p = 0.02).
Negative association between PCB-153 and TBG levels in umbilical cord blood (β = –0.26, p = 0.01).
Negative relationship between maternal PCP and cord fT4 concentrations in neonates (β = –0.59, p = 0.02).
No significant association between PCB-153 and TSH or fT4 in pregnant women.
No association between contaminants and thyroid hormones at 7 months of age.
population: Pregnant Inuit women (mean age 24.9 years) from the three largest communities of the Hudson Bay coast of Nunavik, Quebec, Canada, and their infants during the first year of life (n = 120 mothers, 95 cord samples, 130 infant samples).
exposure_domain: Organochlorine and chlorinated phenolic environmental contaminants (PCBs, hexachlorobenzene, pentachlorophenol, hydroxylated PCB metabolites)
limitations: Small sample sizes, particularly in subsample analyses of cord CPCs.
Loss to follow-up and exclusions reduced analytic sample.
Association between maternal PCP and cord fT4 not corroborated with cord blood PCP despite high correlation (r = 0.85).
